recentItems.title: Taliwas sa sinabi ni Robin: VP Sara walang 'immunity' sa mga kaso ayon sa DOJ
recentItems.description:
Iginiit ni Department of Justice (DOJ) Sec. Fredderick Vida nitong Huwebes (Setyembre 10) na ayon sa umiiral na batas ay ang pangulo lamang ang mayroong immunity mula sa mga kaso.

Ito ay sa kabila ng kasong grave threats na kinakaharap ni Vice President Sara Duterte kaugnay ng umano'y pagbabanta nito sa buhay ni Pangulong Bongbong Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, at dating House Speaker Martin Romualdez.

Sa plenaryo nitong Lunes, iginiit ni Sen. Robin Padilla na dapat mayroon ding "immunity" ang bise tulad ng sa pangulo dahil isa rin aniyang impeachable official si Duterte.

recentItems.title: August was world's joint-hottest month on record, say scientists | ABS-CBN News
recentItems.description:
The world just experienced its joint-hottest month since records began, with August pushing the planet's average global temperature to more than 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, the EU's Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said on Thursday (September 9).

Extreme weather and climate-related disasters raged around the world last month. Scientists have said climate change likely played a role in the landslides and flash floods that killed hundreds in Nepal and China’s Tibet, although the specifics are still being studied. Wildfires surged from Indonesia to Greece and Belgium, while severe drought struck Hungary and Romania.

August 2026 tied with July 2023 as the world's warmest month on record, and was 1.65C hotter than the planet's average temperature in the 19th century, before humans started burning oil, coal and gas on an industrial scale, C3S said.

Emissions from burning these fossil fuels are the main cause of climate change, said scientists. 

"The narrative around climate change has really transitioned from being quite an abstract concept that happens in a faraway place, to disrupting our daily lives," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.

"We've really seen the impact across Europe of how maladapted we are, with roads melting, train lines buckling, schools closing, hospitals completely overwhelmed, and record wildfires for the time of year," she told Reuters.

The data confirmed western Europe is emerging from its hottest summer ever recorded, with many regions suffering unusually low river flows and soil moisture - adding to farmers' woes, after a succession of extreme heatwaves since May ravaged crops.

August was the first month since November 2025 in which the world's average temperature exceeded 1.5C above pre-industrial levels. This is the level of warming which nearly 200 countries vowed under the 2015 Paris climate agreement to try to prevent, to avoid the worst consequences of global warming.

Last month's extreme heat was not limited to land. The world's oceans outside of the polar regions also recorded their joint-highest sea surface temperature for any month on record, C3S said.

In the tropical Pacific, record-high temperatures were fuelled by the formation of the El Nino weather pattern, which is forecast to strengthen in the coming months - potentially pushing global temperatures further higher. — Reuters

(Editing and production: Marta Fiorin)
